headline: CBA's loan impairment expense (LIE) rose $62m or 9% in FY26 to $788m from $726m in FY25 (continuing operations basis). The loss rate increased 1 bpt to 8 bpts of average gross loans and acceptances (GLAA), from 7 bpts. The movement was driven by a $150m rise in net collective provision funding, partly offset by a $17m fall in net new and increased individual provisioning and a $71m increase in write-backs of individually assessed provisions. By division: Retail +$106m to $378m (from $272m), New Zealand +$11m to $66m (from $55m), Corporate Centre +$6m to $1m (from a $5m benefit), partly offset by Business -$45m to $310m (from $355m) and Institutional -$16m to $33m (from $49m). The results presentation corroborates the divisional deltas (RBS +$106m, BB -$45m, IB&M -$16m, NZ +$18m NZD) and the 8 bpts FY26 loss rate.

drivers.narrative: Net collective provision funding rose $150m (606 vs 456). Bank attributes to portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk, macroeconomic uncertainty, and deterioration in the unemployment outlook. Where: Retail +$106m to $378m (from $272m), NZ +$11m to $66m (from $55m) driven by higher collective provisions; Business and Institutional partly offset by higher collective provisions.

drivers.bank_label: Net new and increased individual provisioning
drivers.narrative: Net new and increased individual provisioning fell $17m (422 vs 439). Bank attributes to lower individually assessed provision charges in Business (incl. more write-backs) and release of individually assessed provisions in Institutional; NZ lower individually assessed provisions partly offset.
Write-backs of individually assessed provisions increased $71m (240 vs 169), reducing the charge. Bank cites an increase in write-backs in Business Banking as a driver of its lower expense.

limitations: The three provision-type rows (net collective funding +150, net new/increased individual -17, write-backs -71) sum exactly to the +$62m movement, so residual is zero. Each driver's delta is computed by subtracting the two period levels the bank prints, capping confidence at 80 per the evidence ladder.

The divisional where-layer deltas are all stated by the bank in prose (Retail +106, Business -45, Institutional -16, NZ +11, Corporate Centre +6), corroborated in the results presentation (RBS +106, BB -45, IB&M -16, NZ +18 NZD).
The NZ divisional narrative is reported in NZD (NZD78m, +NZD18m); the A$ divisional table (page 34) shows NZ 66 vs 55, +11, which is used for the where-layer.
Corporate Centre and Other rose $6m to $1m (from a $5m benefit); the bank discloses no reason for this small division.
The loss rate denominator is average gross loans and acceptances (GLAA), per the bank's own definition.
